title: Instrumentation concierge: canonical span token & stable cross-service IDs
creator: Asha Nair
description: Problem: Cross-service trace correlation at Redwood is brittle when clients use different header formats, retry semantics, or when requests fan out asynchronously (queues, websockets, serverless). Existing approaches lead to duplicate or missing spans, confusing join keys in the console, and poor SRE debuggability. Goal: introduce a lightweight SDK/middleware component ("instrumentation concierge") that emits a canonical, stable span token and normalizes incoming propagation headers.
description_more: Scope: SDK client libraries (Node, Python, Go), edge middleware for HTTP/gRPC ingress, and worker/queue adapters. The component will: 1) normalize common incoming headers (traceparent, baggage, X-Trace-* variants), 2) generate a canonical span token header (X-RI-SpanToken) deterministically from the incoming trace context + service-specific salt, 3) preserve sampling decision and causal parent pointers, 4) provide a compatibility mapping layer that rewrites legacy headers for downstream services that haven't adopted X-RI-SpanToken. Non-goals: full replacement of OpenTelemetry propagation formats or changing backend storage keys; compatibility first, migration path second.
implementation_notes: Architecture: small thin library in each SDK that runs before request encoding. Token algorithm: HMAC-SHA256 over (incoming-span-id|parent-id|service-id|request-id) using a per-environment salt stored in KMS (rotatable). Token length: 16 bytes base64url to keep header size small. Backwards compatibility: if X-RI-SpanToken present, preserve it; otherwise create and inject and also emit legacy headers for services behind a migration flag. Sampling: maintain existing sampling header (X-RI-Sample) and ensure consistent propagation. Performance target: median token emit cost <200ns on hot path; end-to-end <0.5% p99 latency uplift. We'll implement native bindings for Go and lightweight JS/Python versions. Edge middleware will provide header-normalization for non-upgraded clients and an opt-out config for customers who want raw headers.
observability_and_monitoring: Dashboards/metrics to add: span_token_generation_latency_ms (p50/p90/p99), token_collision_count, header-normalization-rate, legacy-header-injection-rate, propagation_loss_rate (requests that exit service without canonical token). New log fields: ri.span_token, ri.token_version. Alerting: firing if token_collision_rate > 1e-6 or propagation_loss_rate increases by >5% vs baseline. Queries and dashboard mocks are in the Confluence design doc.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests covering header permutations, collision fuzzing harness with 10M random contexts, e2e trace stitching tests against the console, and a loadbench job to measure CPU/latency overhead. We'll run canary on internal services (telemetry ingestion, console backend) for 2 weeks, then expand to beta customers. Add regression evals to ensure no change to sampled trace counts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): integrate into SDKs and internal infra, 2-week canary on telemetry ingestion (team: observability). Phase 2 (beta): opt-in flag for customers, migrate clients that opt in. Phase 3 (global): default-on and edge middleware switches to inject legacy headers only when downstream detects non-adoption. Provide migration checklist for Platform/SEs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: token collisions or deterministic token revealing sensitive identifiers. Mitigations: HMAC with KMS-managed salt, fixed-length truncated output, collision fuzzing, and a failsafe that falls back to legacy header if collision detected. Risk: perf impact under high QPS -> mitigate by optimized native code paths and batch token caching for repeated prefixes.
